title: Buy Me a Tea
description: Buy Me a Tea, or شاي واحد in Arabic, is an Egyptian equivalent to the globally known Buy Me a Coffee platform. It provides a direct digital space where independent creators, freelance designers, artists, and writers can receive micro-donations and ongoing support from followers who appreciate their craft. In Egypt, coffee culture is popular, but sharing a hot glass of tea is the authentic daily ritual that binds people together across neighborhoods and creative studios.

Creating an indigenous creator economy brand required translating tipping from an imported Western mechanism into a familiar, natural Egyptian expression of appreciation. Rather than presenting support as a cold transactional donation, the platform frames it as an invitation to pull up a chair, sit down together, and buy a friend a cup of tea. It celebrates everyday creative labor while making digital patron payments accessible, culturally relatable, and warmly community-centered.
direction: The direction here is a different language, but also a different culture. Freelancing is still a relatively new concept in Egypt, without the decades of familiarity it has elsewhere. A platform meant to serve that community had to feel young, loud, and alive, something that speaks directly to a generation figuring out this path for itself.

That's why the identity leans fully into bold, dominant color and an illustrative, hand drawn hand. From the tea glass mark to the wordmark itself, everything is built by hand rather than through rigid grid systems, deliberately a little chaotic. That chaos does two things at once: it grabs a young audience's attention in a crowded feed, and more importantly, it resembles the freelance artist's craft itself, the whole thing feels like a handcrafted artboard. Which it actually is, the entire logo is fully hand drawn, just executed digitally.
